THE ASSUMPTIONS, IN THE OPEN

Real sessions. A modeled alternative.

01

Reported energy and connection.

Dataset 1 provides plug-in time, unplug time, and charger energy. No additional charging losses are added. The first and last five-minute intervals are prorated to the exact connection boundaries. Missing unplug times and uncertain daylight-saving times are excluded.

02

Norwegian habits, ComEd scenario.

Source times use Europe/Oslo. For the chosen ComEd year, each session maps to the nearest same weekday within its source month. The Chicago plug-in clock and original elapsed duration are preserved. Sessions are independent scenarios, not a simultaneous fleet or observed Illinois bills.

03

Useful estimates, clearly labeled.

Dataset 2 estimates user charging power and capacity. Dataset 3 estimates state of charge and idle time, assuming a 95% end state. Dataset 4 validates session energy totals. These are derived estimates, not measured battery traces or electricity-price forecasts.

04

Retrospective scheduling.

Each plan knows the reported energy requirement and unplug deadline. User estimates may use the full source history. This tests scheduling with known needs; it does not validate advance predictions. Power is never raised to hide a shortfall. Only equal-energy completed comparisons count. Standard delivery isolates timing; time-of-day also changes the delivery rate. Fixed study rates exclude flat and capacity charges.

Source: Sørensen, Sartori, Lindberg and Andresen. Published dataset · Methods and assumptions.

01

Your energy stays your energy.

Each row uses kwh_used as grid energy. kwh_added and battery percentages are shown as recorded. No vehicle capacity or extra efficiency loss is assumed.

02

The window matters.

Each row is replayed independently. Charging timestamps are interpreted in America/Chicago and rounded outward to five-minute boundaries. They are charging events, not verified plug-in or unplug times. The morning scenario extends availability to the chosen hour, caps the extension at the next recorded session, and always keeps the original window.

03

Standard versus time-of-day.

The baseline charges immediately on standard delivery. SPARC and the alternative plans default to time-of-day delivery. Savings include both rate and timing changes, with the same grid energy, power, and available window. Selecting standard for the plans isolates timing savings. Savings count only when both finish. The study’s fixed rates apply across all dates; flat bill charges and capacity charges are excluded.

04

Recorded does not mean metered detail.

The recorded-pattern estimate spreads grid energy evenly over each recorded window; the CSV has no interval power trace. Logged CSV cost is shown separately and is not the savings baseline. Peak power below the energy-implied average is raised and flagged. Missing prices and ambiguous daylight-saving timestamps are skipped.
